change.author: nicktrn

findings.title: Backup-code login can skip the password check by also sending a totpCode
findings.body: The password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (lines 121-129). The new backup-code branch at line 131 runs whenever `credentials.backupCode` is set, and never looks at `totpCode`. A direct `signIn`/callback request with `email`, any non-empty `totpCode` (for example "1") and a valid `backupCode` skips password verification, and the TOTP check is also skipped because the backup branch wins. A single static backup code is then enough to sign in. The UI clears `totpCode` before showing the backup form (login.tsx:125), so the normal flow is unaffected; the hole is only reachable by calling the API directly. The TOTP-only bypass already existed, but a backup code is a long-lived static secret, so this widens it. Make the password check also run when a backup code is supplied, for example `if (user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode))`.

findings.title: Closing the dialog on the backup-codes step loses the codes and leaves the UI stale
findings.body: After a successful `enable` call, 2FA is already on in the DB and `onEnable()` is only called from the "Close" button (line 269). The dialog is still wired to `onOpenChange`, so Esc, the X button or a click outside closes it (pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64 just toggles `enableModalOpen`). In that case neither `resetState` nor `onEnable` runs. Three things follow. The user never saw or saved their backup codes, and they are shown only once. `viewer.me` is not invalidated, so the switch and badge keep showing 2FA as disabled until a reload (two-factor-auth.tsx:65-68). The modal stays mounted at `DisplayBackupCodes`, so clicking the switch again reopens it with the old codes, with `password` still set. Handle `onOpenChange` on this step, either by preventing dismissal or by routing it through the same reset-and-`onEnable` path as the Close button.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The code reads the encrypted list, finds the index, then writes back the whole re-encrypted array. Two concurrent logins with the same code can both read it before either write lands, so both succeed and the code is used twice. Concurrent logins with different codes can also overwrite each other, so a used code gets revived. The window is small and needs the attacker to already hold a code. A conditional update (compare the stored `backupCodes` value in the `where`) or a transaction would close it. The same read-compare pattern is in disable.ts, but there the codes are wiped afterwards.

findings.title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive but the UI placeholder is uppercase
findings.body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (setup.ts:61) and compared with an exact `indexOf` (here and at disable.ts:61). The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX` (BackupCode.tsx:21), and nothing lowercases the input. A user who retypes a code in uppercase gets "Backup code is incorrect". Lowercasing the user input before the lookup, or showing codes in uppercase, avoids this. Trimming whitespace would also help for pasted codes.

findings.title: "Please generate them in your settings" points to a feature that does not exist
findings.body: `missing_backup_codes` tells users to generate codes in their settings. This PR adds no regenerate action. Codes are only created in `setup.ts`, which refuses to run while 2FA is enabled (setup.ts:42-44). Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null`. They hit this message, and the only way to get codes is to disable 2FA and enable it again. The message should say that, or a regenerate action should be added.

findings.title: Component is named TwoFactor
findings.body: The default export is called `TwoFactor`, copied from `TwoFactor.tsx`. It is a backup-code input, so the name is misleading in stack traces and devtools. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

findings.title: Copy shows a success toast without waiting for the clipboard write
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught. If it rejects (permissions, insecure context), the user still sees "Backup codes copied!" and may then close the dialog with nothing saved. Await it and show the toast only on success, with an error toast otherwise.

contracts.action: Backup-code login (new credentials field handled in authorize)
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing TOTP branch right below it (lines 157-187) and the password check above it (lines 121-129).
contracts.before_after: Before: password is verified unless totpCode is set, then TOTP is verified. Now: the backup branch runs first when backupCode is set, and it never checks totpCode. It consumes the code via prisma.user.update. Password verification still depends only on !totpCode.
contracts.visible_effect: Login result reaches the UI through signIn's res.error, mapped in login.tsx:156-160 to incorrect_backup_code or missing_backup_codes.
contracts.failure_mode: Request with a non-empty totpCode plus a valid backupCode skips the password check. Concurrent use of one code is not atomic. A decrypt or JSON.parse failure throws a generic error shown as something_went_wrong.

contracts.action: Backup codes displayed after enabling 2FA, with Close, Copy and Download buttons
contracts.equivalent_path: The old flow called onEnable() directly after enable succeeded (replaced at line 135). The parent's onEnable closes the modal and invalidates viewer.me.
contracts.before_after: Before: success on enable led to onEnable(), then modal closed and the switch refreshed. Now: success moves to the DisplayBackupCodes step, and onEnable is only called from the Close button. Dialog dismissal via onOpenChange does not call it.
contracts.visible_effect: The switch/badge refresh only after the Close button. Esc, X or an outside click leaves the badge stale and the codes lost.
contracts.failure_mode: Dismissing the dialog on this step leaves 2FA enabled in the DB, codes never saved, and the modal stuck on the backup-codes step with stale state when reopened. Buttons default to type="button" (Button.tsx:125), so they do not submit the enclosing Form.

contracts.equivalent_path: The existing TOTP branch in the same handler (lines 69-100).
contracts.before_after: The password check runs first (lines 40-45), then the backup-code lookup. On success all backup codes and the secret are cleared in the final update (line 107). The modal sends backupCode, and resetForm clears fields when toggling between TOTP and backup code.
contracts.visible_effect: DisableTwoFactorModal maps IncorrectBackupCode and MissingBackupCodes to messages. A 200 response calls onDisable.
contracts.failure_mode: A non-string backupCode in the body makes replaceAll throw, giving a 500. The encryption-key failure uses throw rather than a 500 JSON response, matching the existing TOTP branch.

contracts.action: Setup endpoint generates and stores backup codes and returns them in the response
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing secret generation and encrypted storage in the same handler (lines 58, 70).
contracts.before_after: The codes are encrypted with symmetricEncrypt like the secret. They are stored while twoFactorEnabled is still false, and returned in plaintext once.
contracts.visible_effect: The Enable modal stores them in state and shows them after the TOTP step.
contracts.failure_mode: If the user cancels before finishing, orphaned codes stay in the DB until the next setup overwrites them, which is harmless. Repeated setup calls regenerate the codes, which is fine while 2FA is disabled.

summary:
I found two problems that should be fixed in this PR and several smaller ones.

- **Password bypass:** a login request with a non-empty `totpCode` and a valid `backupCode` skips password verification in `next-auth-options.ts`. The UI clears `totpCode`, so only direct API calls reach it.
- **Backup codes lost on dismiss:** closing the Enable dialog on the backup-codes step (Esc, the X button, or a click outside) never calls `onEnable`. The user does not get to save the codes, the 2FA switch stays stale, and the modal reopens on the old step.
- **Smaller points:** backup code use is not atomic, comparison is case-sensitive while the placeholder is uppercase, the `missing_backup_codes` message points to a regenerate option that does not exist, the new component is still named `TwoFactor`, and the copy toast fires without waiting for the clipboard write.

I read all 16 files and did not run or build anything.
